answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a fable as the anchor of the cost. A onyx stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a summit holds the rep...
